text:
[LTIM.2.8.4] **One sample per step.** The engine **must** sample both clocks
together when it consumes an input and when a pump begins, and **must not** read
either clock at any other time. Every read between two samples — in a `where`
condition, a re-evaluation, a `let`, an action — returns the most recent
sample. Two reads of `now()`, or of `monotonic_ns()`, between the same two
samples therefore return the same value, whatever order the engine evaluates
the expressions containing them in and however many times it evaluates each.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_1__tick_called
idris.note: A tick: Rete/NetworkTimed.idr's; the call trackers stand.

idris.name: Ltim_2_4_1__ttest
idris.note: A test of the held sample: its arguments are the sample and the stamps, never a clock.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_1__at_sample
idris.note: THE SUBSTITUTION: every clock leaf replaced by its literal under the sample and the stamps, the rest of the expression as it is, so that the plain evaluator reads no clock. The sample a read sees is the one the state holds: 'every read between two samples returns the most recent sample'.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_1__clock_free_unchanged
idris.note: A `where` with no clock read reads no sample: substituting the held sample into it is the identity, for every sample.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_1__tests_at
idris.note: The tests at the held wall sample: what a pump's re-evaluation reads.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__tick_then_pump_is_clocked
idris.note: The sample a pump's re-evaluation reads is the tick's: one sample from the tick through the pump.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__tick_timed
idris.note: A TICK: the clock takes the sample and the sweep runs; the wall sample, the stamps and the trackers stand. LESS than the clause: the tick is the Idris model's sample point and the monotonic half alone moves (the wall is R4b's); the data inputs and the pump that follow read the sample it took.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__tick_timed_projects
idris.note: A TICK PROJECTS to Rete/NetworkCooldown.idr's prepared tick: the stamps and the wall ride beside.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_6__input_timed
idris.note: A data input runs at the held sample. LESS than the clause: it samples nothing new -- a data input moves no clock in this model, the Idris model's cadence sampling at the tick.

idris.name: ltac_3_3__stamp_is_fire_at
idris.note: `monotonic_ns()` read in the firing is the sample the pump holds, which is the stamp: one sample per pump.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_4__timed
idris.note: A time-dependent join test over the sample: `now()` reads the wall sample, `monotonic_ns()`, `dwell` and `within` the monotonic one.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__apply_sampled
idris.note: A DATA INPUT at the held sample: Rete/NetworkTtl.idr's apply on the engine, and the stamps as Rete/EntryStamp.idr's assert has them, at the held monotonic sample, on the engine's working memory. A retraction stamps nothing. A data input moves no clock in this model.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__at_wall
idris.note: A two-clock test at a fixed wall sample is a test on the monotonic clock alone: what Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's engine takes.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__counts_sampled
idris.note: The firings of a history of samples, one count per pump.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__counts_sampled_cons
idris.note: One pump of a sample history, unfolded.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__counts_sampled_held_wall
idris.note: The held wall sample is read by nothing on this engine: a history's counts from two states that differ in it alone are one list, since the tests read the sample a pump is given. A TRANSCRIPTION of `pump_sampled`'s definition, `Refl`; it fails if the pump is made to read the state's wall and refutes nothing else.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__pump_sampled
idris.note: THE PUMP AT A SAMPLE: Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's pump at `Tick m` with the tests fixed at `w`; the wall sample kept; the stamps untouched, since a tick asserts nothing. With the halt and the count.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__pump_sampled_parts
idris.note: The pump at a sample, as the composed pump: its three parts.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__run_from
idris.note: THE RECORDING ENGINE, generic in what a step does: the source is called once as each step begins, and the step runs under that sample.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__step_sampled
idris.note: The state after the pump at a sample.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__tests_at
idris.note: The tests of an engine, each read from the stamp table it holds, each fixed at a wall sample.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__triple
idris.note: A triple is its three parts: how a proof names a pump's result without abstracting the pump from its goal.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_4__expr
idris.note: An expression that may read the clocks: `now()`, `monotonic_ns()`, a value that reads neither, and any binary operation over two of these. The operator is a parameter, so what is proved of `Bin` holds of every operator.

idris.name: Ltim_2_8_4__reader
idris.note: How a clock read is served: from the count of source calls made so far, the sample the read sees and the count afterwards.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__eval
idris.note: EVALUATION AS AN ENGINE DOES IT: operand by operand in an order (left operand first, or right), each clock read served by the reader, the count of source calls threaded through.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__fresh
idris.note: THE REFUSED READER: a read calls the clock source, a reading the clause refuses.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__fresh_calls_twice
idris.note: AND IT CALLS THE SOURCE: two reads, two calls, by computation.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__fresh_differs_by_order
idris.note: THE REFUSED READER IS ORDER-DEPENDENT: reading the source at every read, `now() - now()` is 0 with the left operand first and 1 with the right. The engine's evaluation order has become an observable, which one sample per step rules out. A refutation of the refused reading, not of the clause.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__held
idris.note: THE CLAUSE'S READER: a read returns the held sample and calls the source not at all -- 'returns the most recent sample'.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__held_calls_nothing
idris.note: AND THE SOURCE IS NOT CALLED: the count after evaluation is the count before it, for an expression of any size. 'Must not read either clock at any other time'.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__held_orders_agree
idris.note: HOWEVER MANY TIMES: the two orders agree with each other from any two call counts, so an engine that evaluates one expression twice, in two orders, at two points of a step, reads one value.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__held_value
idris.note: ONE VALUE, WHATEVER THE ORDER: under a held sample, evaluation in either order and from any call count yields what the expression is worth under that sample -- for every expression, every operator, every sample. 'Whatever order the engine evaluates the expressions containing them in'.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__now_minus_now
idris.note: `now() - now()`. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__samples
idris.note: The samples a run holds, one per step: the source is called once as each step begins. A step is a sample point of either kind the clause names -- an input consumed or a pump begun -- and the model does not distinguish the two nor say anything of what a step does between its sample and the next; only that it samples once.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__worth
idris.note: What an expression is worth under one sample: the clause's definition, in which no evaluation order and no read count appears.
